input: Merge email addresses from /data/list1.txt, /data/list2.txt, and /data/list3.txt into a single deduplicated, alphabetically sorted list. Save it to /data/combined.txt and print the total count of unique emails.

transcript.final_response:
I combined the three lists into `/data/combined.txt`, removed duplicates and sorted the result alphabetically.

**Total unique emails: 6**

```
alice@example.com
bob@example.com
charlie@example.com
dave@example.com
eve@example.com
frank@example.com
```

The three files had 9 emails in total, 3 of which were repeats: bob was in lists 1 and 2, alice in lists 1 and 3, and eve in lists 2 and 3. I checked the files first, and none of them had stray spaces, Windows line endings or uppercase letters that could hide a duplicate.
tool_calls: cd /data; for f in list1.txt list2.txt list3.txt; do echo "== $f"; cat -A "$f" | head -50; wc -l "$f"; done
cd /data; cat list1.txt list2.txt list3.txt | sort -u > combined.txt; cat combined.txt; echo "Total unique emails: $(wc -l < combined.txt)"
